description: The Interceptor API agreement implemented by Operator integrations. This is neither a target capability manifest nor an inventory of administrative commands, providers, services or Interceptor-only configuration.

transport.boundary: Operator and Interceptor share a trusted host. The existing loopback HTTP listener is the integration boundary; campaign IDs scope access but do not authenticate hostile local callers.
transport.requests: POST with Content-Type: application/json and strict JSON objects. Unknown fields, duplicate keys, trailing values and invalid nesting are rejected.
transport.responses: JSON GatewayResponse {status, body, session_revision}; HTTP status follows native status except 204 is wrapped using HTTP 200. Successful evidence download is binary.
transport.errors: JSON body.code identifies errors. Parse/route errors include 400 invalid_request, 405 method_not_allowed, 413 frame_too_large and 404 not_found. Endpoint-specific errors below are representative; the referenced implementations define the complete codes. Never treat an unfamiliar error as success.
transport.native_operation_rules: Non-HTTP operation names below select request.operation in the native envelope. session.stop is deliberately unavailable on this route; use lifecycle operation=session.stop. Public session.owner only closes execution; attach owns binding.
transport.bounds: Use existing wire parsing and transport bounds in the referenced codecs. Resource budgets, timeouts and runtime policy remain Interceptor-owned and are not fixed compatibility requirements.

capabilities.description: Discover the supported Operator API agreement before attachment
inputs: Empty JSON object {}
outputs: body.interceptor_contract_version: exact major.minor.patch string
body.interceptor_contract_sha256: 64 lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digits over the entire embedded UTF-8 contract document, including whitespace and its final newline
errors: 400 invalid_request for invalid JSON or nonempty requests; 405 method_not_allowed; 413 frame_too_large
guarantees: Read-only, no campaign or target access, no runtime reconciliation; Cache-Control: no-store
Operator compares both the returned version and document SHA-256 with its independently pinned supported version and hash before attachment; mismatch or unreadable identity stops campaign execution
The hash identifies the contract document, not an executable, release archive, capability manifest, API response or canonicalized subset; its value is not embedded in the document itself

Both version and exact document hash must match, including after formatting-only edits; pins are never learned from the running service; no source-commit pin, Internet lookup or user-supplied document is required

capabilities.description: Associate the instance with one campaign and obtain the active binding
inputs: AttachRequest: api_version=interceptor.dev/local-lifecycle/v1alpha1, campaign_id, worker_instance_id; optional allow_target_stop (default false)
outputs: body.api_version; campaign_id; binding {session_id, worker_instance_id, run_revision}; session metadata; capabilities containing the native environment CapabilityManifest; evidence_max_bytes
prerequisites: Successful compatibility check; running Interceptor instance with a ready target
errors: 400 invalid_attach; 409 campaign_mismatch, campaign_policy_conflict or instance_not_ready; 503 instance_store_unavailable or session_unavailable; native bind/capability errors may propagate
guarantees: Campaign and stop policy persist for this process lifetime; same-campaign reattachment preserves the current session and policy
Worker identity is caller attribution, not exclusive ownership; attachment does not reopen closed execution

capabilities.description: Submit native experiment requests through the integrated API
inputs: OperationEnvelope with exactly request and body; request uses interceptor.dev/operation-request/v1alpha2

request fields: request_id, operation_id, operation, session_id, campaign_id, worker_instance_id, positive run_revision, body_digest and deadline; expected_session_revision for mutations; attempt_id and attempt_context_digest where required
body is the operation-specific JSON object; body_digest hashes its exact embedded UTF-8 bytes
outputs: GatewayResponse: status, body and session_revision; operation-specific success or body.code error; native 204 uses HTTP 200 framing
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 400 invalid_request; 403 campaign_mismatch; 409 session_not_in_campaign, stale_session or execution_unavailable_or_closed
400 use_lifecycle_stop for native session.stop; 400 use_attach_to_bind for public owner binding
503 session_unavailable_outcome_unknown indicates uncertainty, not proof of non-execution
guarantees: Only native operations listed below are supported; there is no shell, host-path selection, remote provisioning or arbitrary forwarding API
Mutations address the active session and compare its native revision; reads may address retained campaign sessions
Exact retries reuse command identity and return recorded outcomes; changed command fields conflict; worker/run-revision attribution changes alone do not create a new effect
Reconcile uncertain outcomes with operation.status rather than replaying with a fresh identity
Closure is terminal; bounded injection cleanup and reads remain subject to campaign and integrity checks

capabilities.description: Restore a checkpoint or confirm target termination
inputs: LifecycleRequest: api_version=interceptor.dev/local-lifecycle/v1alpha1, campaign_id, worker_instance_id, positive run_revision, current session_id, operation_id and operation
operation=snapshot.restore requires checkpoint_id; optional source_session_id selects a retained campaign session
operation=session.stop omits checkpoint_id and source_session_id and requires attach-time allow_target_stop
outputs: Restore: replacement binding and session metadata; stop: session_id and phase=stopped; 202 operation_in_progress for an admitted duplicate
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 400 invalid_lifecycle_request; 403 campaign_mismatch or target_stop_not_permitted
409 operation_conflict, stale_session, source_session_not_in_campaign or execution_unavailable_or_closed; 429 lifecycle_capacity_exhausted
503 instance_store_unavailable, target_stop_unconfirmed, restore_failed or lifecycle_outcome_unknown; reconcile via status
guarantees: Admitted operations survive caller disconnects; retry the same operation identity or query status
Restore validates source state and checkpoint, closes and stops the old target, creates a fresh session, advances run_revision and rebinds the campaign
Explicit campaign closure cannot be reopened by restore; failed restoration never reports a successful replacement
Stop success requires host-confirmed termination; it is distinct from merely closing native execution admission

capabilities.description: Read instance lineage or reconcile lifecycle work
inputs: api_version=interceptor.dev/local-lifecycle/v1alpha1, campaign_id; optional operation_id
outputs: Without operation_id: instance_id, campaign_id, active binding, sessions, phase, closed, store_available, evidence_max_bytes and failure
With operation_id: lifecycle Record containing original request, fingerprint, state and response
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 403 campaign_mismatch; 404 operation_not_recorded for unknown lifecycle identity
guarantees: Reporting remains available after closure; unknown records do not prove that an operation had no effects
Native operations use operation.status; this route reconciles the separate lifecycle ledger

capabilities.description: List or inspect retained campaign checkpoints
inputs: SnapshotListRequest: lifecycle api_version, campaign_id; optional source_session_id, offset and limit
SnapshotInspectRequest: lifecycle api_version, campaign_id, source_session_id and checkpoint_id
outputs: List: campaign_id, checkpoints, total and optional next_offset; inspect: the verified checkpoint metadata
Checkpoint metadata includes source session/campaign identity, checkpoint identity, label, description and integrity data
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: Malformed requests, invalid pagination, foreign sessions, missing checkpoints or corrupt checkpoint data return errors; see snapshot route definitions
guarantees: Reads use retained host records and never restart or contact the target; inventory remains separate from snapshot creation and restoration

capabilities.description: Download independently collected evidence for a stopped campaign session
inputs: api_version=interceptor.dev/local-lifecycle/v1alpha1, campaign_id, session_id
outputs: Successful binary application/x-tar response; X-Content-SHA256 identifies the evidence bytes; X-Evidence-Max-Bytes communicates the configured acceptance bound
Archive contains protected session evidence, integrity records, execution outcomes and completeness information
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 403 session_not_in_campaign; 409 evidence_unavailable_or_target_not_stopped; 413 evidence_limit_exceeded with evidence_retained=true; 503 evidence_read_failed
guarantees: No caller-chosen export path; export does not restart a stopped target
Consumers verify archive integrity and completeness rather than equating a successful download with a successful experiment
Required evidence failures cannot be reported as complete success; agent-authored claims are not independent outcome proof

capabilities.description: Read environment-specific availability without conflating it with API compatibility
inputs: Empty body {} in the native operation envelope
outputs: Native CapabilityManifest for the addressed session, including its identity/digest and available interfaces, delivery contracts, injection surfaces and feedback profiles
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: Shared campaign/session and native integrity errors
guarantees: Operator reads this manifest before selecting campaign actions; matching contract versions does not imply every target supports every action
The manifest is a separate build-derived resource; target configuration and available values are not enumerated in this contract; runtime policy still governs admission

capabilities.description: Read native session and operation outcomes
inputs: session.status: {}
operation.status: exactly one of receipt_id (application turn) or operation_id (durable native mutation)
outputs: session.status: {session, owner, execution_available}; session.revision is the native mutation revision
operation.status: native turn for receipt_id, or recorded request/fingerprint/state/response for operation_id
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 400 invalid_operation_lookup; 404 operation_not_recorded_outcome_unknown; receipt/session availability errors
guarantees: A missing record or failed lookup never establishes non-execution; running includes queued work
Retained reporting uses preserved campaign association without restarting the target

capabilities.description: Close campaign execution admission without implicitly stopping the target
inputs: OwnerRequest: action=close_execution, session_id and campaign_id matching the envelope; omit allow_target_stop; optional legacy worker_instance_id is attribution only
outputs: ExecutionOwner directly in body, including campaign attribution, closed_at and closure_reason when present
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: 400 use_attach_to_bind for binding/stop-policy changes; 409 closure_unconfirmed for retained records that cannot prove closure
guarantees: Terminal campaign closure bypasses the mutation queue and revision race; already-dispatched work can finish and remains reportable
No implicit target-stop permission, ownership transfer or reopening; healthy planned restore uses lifecycle instead of prior terminal closure

capabilities.description: Register payload bytes and bind attempt context
inputs: artifact.register: descriptor and base64 content; descriptor declares digest, size_bytes, media_type and canonicalization
artifact.read: digest
attempt.register: native AttemptContext with campaign, attempt lineage, payload descriptor, generator, feedback profile and timestamp; envelope attempt_id and attempt_context_digest must match
outputs: Registered artifact descriptor or attempt context; artifact.read returns digest and base64 content
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: Invalid descriptors/digests, content-integrity failures, attempt_binding_mismatch, conflicting identities or exhausted native capacity are rejected
guarantees: Artifacts and attempts are scoped to the campaign and integrity-checked before dependent actions; registration does not authorize arbitrary target operations

capabilities.description: Arm declared injection surfaces or delete a campaign injection
inputs: injection.arm: native definition and optional eligible_turn; registered attempt identity/digest in the envelope; fresh injection ID
definition uses a surface, selector, payload and constraints available in the environment capability manifest
injection.delete: injection_id; no original arm record or attempt context required
outputs: Arm: injection receipt/definition; delete: native completion; delivery and committed outcomes are established separately through observations/evidence
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: invalid_injection, injection_id_already_exists, attempt_binding_mismatch, unsupported surfaces or policy constraints
Delete: confirmed missing injection is 404 not_found; persistence failure is 500 injection_delete_failed
guarantees: Deleting an injection does not undo previous effects; restored injections remain eligible for campaign-scoped cleanup
Response alteration is distinct from persisted state alteration and does not prove committed target changes
No service implementation inventory is implied; Operator selects actions using the environment manifest

capabilities.description: Invoke a declared target operation under registered attempt attribution
inputs: TurnRequest: operation and input bytes (base64 JSON), media_type, attempt_id, payload_digest; supported legacy HTTP fields and artifact_digest follow the native TurnRequest definition
Registered attempt matching envelope attempt_id and attempt_context_digest; operation/input contract selected from the environment manifest
outputs: Native turn receipt and status; operation.status retrieves completion and output; observations are read separately
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: invalid_application_invocation, attempt_binding_mismatch, unsupported operation/input contract, closed execution, native limit errors or evidence_storage_error
guarantees: Supervisor-observed activity is attributed to the active invocation window, never trusted from target-supplied attribution headers
Runtime/provider configuration stays with Interceptor; this API does not select a model provider or alter application launch configuration

capabilities.description: Read permitted observations and bounded content for an attempt
inputs: observation.read: turn_id or receipt_id, mutually exclusive; empty lookup only when unambiguous
observation.content.read: receipt_id, entry_id, offset and max_bytes
Both requests bind the registered attempt using envelope attempt_id and attempt_context_digest
outputs: Observation view with receipts, permitted entries and feedback; content read returns the selected bounded chunk, entry identity and position
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: invalid_observation_request, invalid_observation_read, attempt_binding_mismatch; unknown, ambiguous or unauthorized receipt/content access is rejected
guarantees: Feedback profiles filter disclosure; fixed receipts prevent widening the view with later reads
Observed attribution describes the invocation window; outcome verdicts come from independent observations/oracles, not agent-authored claims

capabilities.description: Capture supported logical sandbox and application state
inputs: Optional label, description and maximum_committed_bytes; campaign identity comes from the envelope, not a body override
outputs: Verified checkpoint identity and metadata, including campaign ID and description covered by the checkpoint hash
prerequisites: Attached campaign; session belongs to that campaign; shared request rules apply
errors: invalid_snapshot_request, snapshot capability/quiesce failures, snapshot_bytes_exhausted or evidence_storage_error
guarantees: Availability comes from the environment manifest; application memory is restorable only through the declared state contract, not process-memory capture
Caller byte allowance can only tighten native limits; zero is exhausted; failed or oversized snapshots are not committed
Creation, retained metadata lookup and lifecycle restoration are separate API operations
